name: NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B-4GB

lineage.family: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt (E4B; the 74B-A9B record is a different model)
lineage.how_derived: multi-environment reinforcement learning (GRPO, NeMo RL and NeMo Gym) on Gemma-4-E4B-it for instruction following, multi-step tool use, multi-turn conversation and structured output; the 4GB repo is the BF16 model quantized to Q4_K_M

purpose: NVIDIA states it is designed for fast local voice and device assistants, interactive personas and embedded interfaces, with emphasis on multi-turn tool use, instruction following and input grounding.

license.name: OpenMDW-1.1
license.notes: Read the OpenMDW-1.1 text (github OpenMDW/OpenMDW 1.1, 2026-11-19): permission to deal in the Model Materials without restriction (copyright, patent, database, trade secret) free of charge; distribution must keep the agreement and notices; patent or copyright suit against others terminates the grant; no restrictions on outputs; no warranty. The card says the model was post-trained on Gemma 4 whose terms it names as Apache-2.0.

architecture.drafter: separate DFlash drafter (nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B-4GB-DFlash, 0.74 GB GGUF BF16; llama.cpp --spec-type draft-dflash)
architecture.why_this_design: The card gives no architecture reasons: the model is Gemma-4-E4B-it further post-trained; only the training method (asynchronous RL with GRPO) is described.

variants.notes: 6.2 GB because the Gemma 4 E4B per-layer embeddings are large; hence the '4GB' name refers to the 4B effective parameters

pc-12gb.notes: 6.2 GB file; BF16 16 GB would not fit

other: Ollama (needs the gemma4 renderer and parser re-registered, user report)
engine_support.notes: Card quick start uses llama.cpp server image b11459, also with DFlash drafter; the card table says 'llama.cpp (recipe pending)'. Gemma 4 E4B itself is in the database (gemma-4-e4b-it).

benchmarks.name: Korean document QA, 299 questions, thinking off

strengths: Instruction following and multi-turn constraints much better than the Gemma 4 E4B base (MultiChallenge 55.6 against 39.4, vendor)
Short answers (brevity), reliable JSON in one user's tests
Small and fast enough for voice and device assistants
weaknesses: No gain over Gemma 4 E4B on Korean document QA (independent, not significant)
Long-context and agent tasks behind Qwen3.5 4B in the vendor table (RULER 64K, Tau2, BFCL)
soft.behavior: Thinking via enable_thinking and a runtime thinking budget; conversational_mode template switch; recommended sampling temperature 1.0 top_p 0.95 in both modes; answers are shorter than the base.
avoid_for: coding agents (not a target of the card)

user_reports.summary: Korean document-QA test against the Gemma 4 E4B base: 63.2 vs 65.2 % without thinking, 67.2 vs 69.6 % with thinking, not significant; shorter answers; Ollama needs the gemma4 renderer and parser to enable thinking
Consistently valid JSON even in complex extraction and classification cases

soft.maturity: NVIDIA first-party, technical report and blog linked from the card; 172k downloads of the 4GB repo in about 6 weeks.

tona_fit.reason: A fine small assistant and tool-use model, but its base (Gemma 4 E4B) is already in the database and independent evidence shows little gain beyond instruction following; not a coding model. Permissive license.
blockers: no gemma4 E4B backend in Tona
